subject: Dedicated capacity heatmap & KV cache / precision impact
messages:
From: Olivia Zhang <olivia.z@aurixa.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@polybio.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Dec 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity planning ask: 32k context, KV reuse patterns

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Were moving toward a committed Dedicated deployment and need a realistic capacity heatmap and guidance on how precision choices will affect GPU commitments. High-level details: 
- Primary model: med-Large-32k (22B-ish) served for clinical summarization and RAG.
- Typical request: 600 input tokens + 1,500 generated tokens (peak), average generation ~500 tokens.
- Context reuse: ~60% prefix reuse (same patient notes loaded frequently).
- Peak concurrency target: 180 concurrent sessions during a 20-minute daily peak.
- SLO: 95th latency target <350ms (generation tail), higher latencies acceptable for batch backfill.

Questions:
1) How much of our GPU footprint is kv/cache driven vs model weights?
2) What delta in reserved GPUs when moving from fp16 -> int8 -> int4?
3) Practical offload options (KV to host NVMe) and latency tradeoffs?

Can you send an initial heatmap and rough node count we should commit for a 12-month retainer? Would like the draft today if possible.

Thanks,
Olivia
Olivia Zhang
Head of ML Ops, Aurixa Therapeutics
olivia.z@aurixa.com

P.S. attaching our weekly traffic histogram and a sample 24-hour trace (see Drive link).

Olivia —

Appreciate the detail. I attached an initial heatmap (capacity-heatmap-v1.xlsx) and a short model profile (kv-cache-model-profiles.pdf). Key assumptions up front: med-Large-32k ~22B parameters; baseline fp16 memory for model weights ~45GB in working set; KV cache linear with max context. Weve modelled three precision lanes (fp16 / int8 / int4) and two KV strategies: fully in-GPU (lowest latency) and hybrid offload (KV on NVMe with an MRU cache on GPU).

Open questions for sizing:
- Do you need hard tail SLOs for every request or is per-route fallback ok?
- Will you accept a small fraction (5-10%) of requests routed to a higher-latency backfill tier?

If you can confirm Ill finalize a commitment recommendation (node counts, recommended GPU family, and canary policy) and share it to the HubSpot deal record.

-Michael

--

Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: capacity-heatmap-v1.xlsx, kv-cache-model-profiles.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Dec 2028 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity planning ask: 32k context, KV reuse patterns

Looping in Priyom and Laura for the deep-sizing readout. Notes from quick pass on the profile Michael attached: 

1) KV cache math (rough):
- KV growth is linear with sequence length. For med-Large-32k we measured ~0.9-1.2 GB of KV per 1k tokens for the pair (keys+values) under our optimized kernel layout at batch size 1. So 32k context = ~28-38 GB just for KV if everything is kept on-GPU.
- That means for fp16 serving with model weight working set (~45GB) + KV (~30GB) youre east of 70GB working set. H100 80GB can fit that but leaves little headroom for batching.

2) Precision impact on model weights:
- fp16: baseline weight working set ~45GB.
- int8: roughly 2x reduction -> ~22-24GB, plus small dequantization overhead in compute path; gives ~1.7-2x headroom improvement for a given GPU.
- int4: ~3.5-4x reduction in weight footprint vs fp16 -> ~11-13GB, but int4 toolchain has edge cases for some operators and may increase CPU pre/post processing.
- KV cache is not compressed by weight quantization: its runtime activations and stored keys/values, so KV dominates at long contexts.

3) Offload options and latency tradeoffs:
- NVMe-hosted KV with hot MRU on GPU: reduces GPU RAM requirement by ~60-80% for KV but adds 20-120ms per long-history request depending on hit rate and NVMe latency.
- Lossless streaming (reading KV segments on demand) is feasible for background or non-peak flows.

4) Practical recommendation (draft):
- For 95th <350ms with high KV reuse (60%) -> favor H100 80GB with int8 weights. Plan committed pool of 6 H100 nodes to cover steady 120 concurrent low-latency sessions, plus 2 H100 for burst/canary.
- If Aurixa can accept a hybrid tier (5-10% routed to backfill NVMe nodes), we can reduce reserved H100 pool to 4 nodes and rely on elastic burst to cover the peak.

I can convert these into the heatmap that maps concurrency x avg generation length -> node counts. Priyom: please add suggested pod tiling and batch packing parameters (how many concurrent streams per device at the recommended headroom).

-Marcus
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Dec 2028 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity planning ask: 32k context, KV reuse patterns

Marcus / team —

Adding concrete pod sizing and tradeoffs. These are conservative until we do a short smoke run: 

Assumptions: med-Large-32k, 22B param-ish; typical gen 500 tokens; prefix reuse 60%; target 95th latency <350ms.

Pod sizing options (examples):
- H100-80G, int8 weights, KV in-GPU: 1 pod = 8 concurrent steady streams (500-token gens at 30 QPS per pod sustained), headroom 1.4x for bursts.
- H100-80G, int8 weights, hybrid NVMe offload (60% hit MRU): 1 pod = 14 concurrent steady streams but tail latency for long-history hits increases by ~40-80ms.
- A100-80G (older): similar for fp16 but due to higher compute inefficiencies we model ~25% fewer steady streams vs H100 for same config.

Commit recommendation for 12-month retainer (covers steady + 25% headroom + reserve canary capacity):
- Conservative (lowest risk): 8 x H100-80G pods (int8, KV in-GPU).
- Hybrid (cost-optimized): 5 x H100-80G (int8) + 3 x NVMe-backed pods for overflow/backfill.

Notes on operational controls to reduce committed count:
- Aggressive prefix caching at the service layer (cache keys per patient) can push effective KV hit rate from 60% -> 78% and cut GPU KV footprint materially.
- Batching policy: continuous batching with 20-40ms pack window reduces per-token cost; for Aurixa we recommended a 25ms pack window as a compromise.
- Canary and rollback: start commit at the Hybrid configuration, measure real-world hit rates for 2 weeks, then ladder to Conservative if tail SLOs arent met.

Action items:
- Marcus: produce final heatmap matrix mapping concurrent sessions (50/100/150/180) x avg gen length (250/500/1500) -> node counts for both Conservative and Hybrid.
- Michael: I'll draft pricing delta between configurations for the HubSpot record.
- Laura: please confirm whether Aurixa requires HIPAA-specific retention/archival configs that change NVMe encryption profile.

-Priyom
From: Olivia Zhang <olivia.z@aurixa.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@polybio.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Dec 2028 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning ask: 32k context, KV reuse patterns

Thanks team — this is great and very actionable. A few quick clarifications: 
- We can tolerate 5% routed to backfill tier during daily peak.
- Well prioritize int8 as a default (we have some internal tests for int4, but not yet production grade).
- HIPAA: yes, NVMe must be encrypted and key access audited but endpoint residency on NVMe is acceptable.

Next steps: please send a formal proposal with (a) Hybrid commit option and (b) Conservative commit option, each with monthly committed node counts, estimated monthly usage, and an implementation checklist for the first 30 days (canary policy, smoke-run plan, SLA ramp). If possible, include a line item for an initial 2-week pilot (elastic usage) so we can validate real-world KV hit rate — wed like pricing for that too.

If you can get a proposal into HubSpot by EOD tomorrow well move to contracting.

Olivia
